the study of the origin of life, and the search for life on other planets, and the development of innovative analytical strategies to track and characterize the organic compounds in the rock record.

this work provides the first demonstration that S-FTIR imaging combined with chemometrics can be used to identify organic molecules at the micrometric scale in a complex geological context.
our results provide evidence for a potential prebiotic synthesis of organic molecules in the oceanic lithosphere.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed an innovative strategy to detect and characterize organic compounds in complex rocks.

the combination of multivariate data analysis techniques with synchrotron-based infrared imaging is a powerful approach to extract and quantify pure organic and mineral components in complex geological materials.

the serpentinization of oceanic rocks is a key mechanism for the preservation of organic compounds and that the use of multivariate chemometrics applied to S-FTIR data is an efficient tool for the characterization of organic compounds in complex rocks and for the identification of their spatial distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemometric analysis applied to S-FTIR images is a very promising strategy to track organic compounds at the micron scale in complex geological materials.
the combination of S-FTIR and multivariate analysis can be used to track and characterize the distribution of organic compounds at the micrometric scale in complex geological samples.
hyperspectral imaging combined with chemometrics can be used to track the distribution of organic components at the micron scale in complex rocks.
